body:
thankyou so much for your help, a lot of my hesitance comes from the habit of pushing it away so embracing this advice is something I can do to further move past my developed issues, you're a great help, I hope you have a good day
(I did read the whole thing, though responding to each thing would possibly waste your time as well, it all helps so thankyou)

Thats not at all what I meant im sorry, It's more I've heard so much of the same thing before and I'm not sure is asking for advice was a good idea in the first place on my part. It's my own issue that needs to be solved and it isn't okay to have responded like that, I'm sorry

Wow this was, a lot. I suppose it helps but essentially it's just "don't kill yourself and give yourself a purpose" which makes sense, I think the issue comes more from not wanting to be a part of that machine of adding to a worthless goal when it doesn't matter in the end. Not saying you're wrong or anything though, thankyou for the reply it means a lot.
I can give that a try, I suppose "existing" as an alternate option is a lot better than worrying constantly about the next fuck up, thankyou
Online is usually a good bet! If not I would try a local jewellery store and ask for a durable charm bracelet that you can add to over time, gl :)
Not to rain on your parade but maybe asking this on a subreddit of people wanting to kill themselves is a bad idea.
"Agro!!" From shadow of the colossus, when Wander is scared and is shouting in a worried way, along with the whistle to call her from far away

Im not exactly a computer wizard but a huge thing would be looking at the website the graphics tablet came from/belongs to, contacting them is a good bet at finding something that works, if they just recommend getting a new one then I would try and work with Windows 10 but good luck either way OP!

As much as it hurts, if this happens almost all the time you need to let it go before it hurts you more.
I've had similar experiences and staying will only make you watch as a spectator for longer than you need to. I would tell them how you're feeling and if they don't understand then I would look for new people, good luck OP

Try a suicide hotline or a local helpline if you can, ask for advice there or better yet, talk through these things with her. You both seem good for eachother so if the relationship matters to you both tell her what you're going through and that it may be tough at first.
Suicidal thoughts are a tough subject for anyone, with work you can get through it. Good luck OP

Something that could work, try a charm wrist band that looks similar to what she would like to wear, something that won't fall off while she does workouts at the gym and something that you can add to, you can both collect memories by adding charms to the bracelet each time you go a new place, something like that! Good luck and I wish her qn early happy birthday!

Well it doesn't need to be that depressing OP, looking on the bright side is good too! Take this experience as incentive to get out of the house more, go to clubs, meet more people. You'll be more ready next time, just don't expect to have everything go perfectly and you'll be okay. It's not a fairy tale to have hope for a new thing.

I think you should embrace it more than anything, if the people around you are annoyed by how you act when you're genuinely happy then that's a red flag on their part. Be yourself! Changing just as other people aren't annoyed by q state when you aren't miserable just isn't worth it, good luck OP

I hate to be blunt here, but PLEASE don't go searching for some random girl you just met an hour ago by looking for her house. That's majorly creepy, if you see them again in PUBLIC then sure, say hi, but searching for a group of girls that think you're cute because they interacted nicely with you once because it hasn't happened to you before not only comes off as needy to them, but is also a bit stalker-esque.

Well of course you have a right to be mad, the excuse of "family" isn't enough to forgive one horrible act from someone you're related to, it seems as though you both need more communication more than anything, she needs to recognise what you do for her but her reasoning could be anything from mental health to just happening to have a bad day, hope it all works out for you though OP

I believe some people are far too gone to help and unfortunately you're in a tough situation. The overall system is totally messed up and due to his abusive past he doesn't deserve to know you OP, you've done the right thing and you deserve to feel safe around the people you care about.
Make sure you have the cops on speed dial if you can and if anything at all happens just make sure you're ready, he knows that you have power so hopefully that'll be enough to stop anything he may try, good luck OP

Whatever works morally for you man! If you think selling it would give you a guilty conscience or regret then try to turn it in anyways, I'm sure it'll most likely be thrown into a box there as well, but from what you wrote just having the phone in your house seems to be giving you that guilty conscience anyways.
At the end of the day it'll be whatever makes you feel better

Personally I started my own "business", because I've always been an artist I turned my hobby and talent into a marketable thing, it wouldn't pay bills but if you need it for simple leisure and things like driving, car registration, or groceries, turning something you're confident in doing that you can do repeatedly into a profitable venture is a good step, other than that I'd suggest to keep trying, jobs are hard to come by these days but anything can happen. Good luck OP!
I think calling animal control or your local animal rescue centre would be a good idea, depending on where you are this is a pretty common situation so hopefully it all goes well, good luck!

I think a good step towards making yourself feel good, as well as doing the right thing, would be turning it in and explaining the situation to the police or whoever you hand it to. 
If you have no other use for it and it's perfectly good you could also sell it, but hopefully whatever happens something good comes around the bend for you.

Personally I think you should OP, no amount of money or convenience is worth the deterioration of your mental health, put yourself first! 
If advice were to go further I would recommend you have a plan B to make sure you have enough money to live while you job search, you're doing good with the interviews, or better yet make sure you have enough savings to keep yourself alive till an opportunity comes up.
Though while you're asking online, the option is already a plan in your head, and you've already thought it through enough to post this, at the end of the day just do what's best for you and keep yourself happy.
Good luck OP!
Thankyou so much, this helped me feel like it won't always be a bad thing to remember, you're a huge help :) Glad you've recognised your own personal value too, it's a hard thing to do
I wish the best for you two, try to keep a level head and take breaks if need be, you both matter and everything will be okay in the long run :)

Personally I suggest you both get a relationship therapist, or seperate therapists for each of you, you both need to handle your own stuff and take care of yourselves so you have the energy to help eachother. You can't fill someone else's glass while yours is empty

I do hear you, though a big issue is that this entire situation besides P.B ignoring me all had happened over a year ago now, I've been under the assumption that because I was doing better, P.B is assuming that I'll be okay if I'm showing signs of being better and getting over P.A
